## Natural history notes

A small grass skipper characterized by warm brown to orange-brown wings, pale translucent spots on the forewings, and a broken dark dash or stigma on the male forewing. In Florida, it is found in open grassy habitats such as prairies, marsh edges, fields, roadsides, pine flatwoods, and other sunny areas where grasses and nectar plants are available. Adults visit low flowers for nectar and often perch on grasses or other low vegetation, while the caterpillars feed on grasses and use folded or tied grass blades as shelters during development.
